steps.html:
Forty questions on Chapters 4, 5 and 6. No time limit, feedback as you go, and you can retake it as often as you like.

  • 40 questions · pass mark 70%
  • Grammar from Lessons 13–24
  • Vocabulary from all three wordlists
  • Function and register

steps.title: Lesson 13 · relative clauses
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which sentence says the speaker has only one sister?
options: My sister who lives in Almaty is a doctor.
My sister, who lives in Almaty, is a doctor.
My sister that lives in Almaty is a doctor.
steps.answer: My sister, who lives in Almaty, is a doctor.
steps.why: Commas make the clause non-defining: extra information about the only sister there is.

steps.title: Lesson 13 · relative clauses
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: The house, which was built in 1890, is protected.
The house, that was built in 1890, is protected.
The house that was built in 1890 is protected.
steps.answer: The house, that was built in 1890, is protected.
steps.why: That cannot introduce a non-defining clause.

steps.title: Lesson 13 · relative clauses
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'The couple ___ flat we rented were very helpful.'
steps.why: Whose marks possession, including for people.

steps.title: Lesson 13 · relative clauses
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which relative pronoun can be left out?
options: The man who lives upstairs is away.
The flat which we rented was tiny.
The book, which won a prize, is out of print.
steps.answer: The flat which we rented was tiny.
steps.why: You can drop the pronoun only when it is the object of the clause.

steps.title: Lesson 15 · articles
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: '___ courses are open to anyone.'
steps.why: All the + a defined group; all of the is also possible, the all is not.

steps.title: Lesson 15 · quantifiers
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: There were much people at the meeting.
There were many people at the meeting.
There were a much of people at the meeting.
steps.answer: There were many people at the meeting.
steps.why: Many with countable nouns, much with uncountable.

steps.title: Lesson 15 · connected speech
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Fluent speech is hard to catch mainly because …
options: words run into one another, so the boundaries have to be worked out
the grammar changes when people speak fast
steps.answer: words run into one another, so the boundaries have to be worked out
steps.why: Difficulty in fluent speech is almost never lexical.

steps.title: Lesson 14 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A building where residents have private flats but share a kitchen, laundry and garden is …
steps.why: Co-housing: private homes plus deliberately shared facilities.

steps.title: Lesson 16 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: When rising rents push long-time residents out of a district, that district is being …
steps.why: Gentrified.

steps.title: Lesson 16 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Somewhere cheap enough for ordinary people to buy is …
steps.why: Affordable.

steps.title: Lesson 16 · function
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You are starting a conversation with a stranger at a conference. Which opens best?
options: Have you come far for this?
What do you think of the government?
steps.answer: Have you come far for this?
steps.why: Safe topics first: journey, place, the event itself.

steps.title: Lesson 17 · future forms
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You have already arranged it with your employer. Which is best?
options: I'll take three weeks off in July.
I'm taking three weeks off in July.
I take three weeks off in July.
steps.answer: I'm taking three weeks off in July.
steps.why: Present continuous for a fixed arrangement.

steps.title: Lesson 17 · future forms
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You decide at the moment of speaking. Which is best?
options: I'm going to help you with that.
steps.why: Will for a decision made as you speak.

steps.title: Lesson 17 · future forms
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You can see the evidence in front of you. Which is best?
options: Look at those clouds — it will rain.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
Look at those clouds — it rains.
steps.answer: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
steps.why: Going to for a prediction based on present evidence.

steps.title: Lesson 18 · future perfect and continuous
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'By this time next year I ___ here for a decade.'
steps.why: Future perfect continuous: duration up to a point in the future.

steps.title: Lesson 18 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The researchers' practical suggestion about time was to …
options: sleep an hour longer and start later
take time back from something specific, in writing
steps.answer: take time back from something specific, in writing
steps.why: Their point is that time is not found, it is reallocated deliberately.

steps.title: Lesson 20 · likelihood
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which expresses the highest probability?
options: There's a slight chance it will happen.
steps.why: Bound to is near-certainty.

steps.title: Lesson 20 · likelihood
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: There's a possibility that prices will fall.
There's a possibility of prices will fall.
There's a possibility prices to fall.
steps.answer: There's a possibility that prices will fall.
steps.why: A possibility that + clause, or a possibility of + noun or -ing.

steps.title: Lesson 20 · likelihood
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I'd be amazed if the deadline ___ moved again.'
steps.why: After I'd be amazed if the past form marks distance from reality, not past time.

steps.title: Lesson 19 · reading strategy
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Skimming a text for the main idea means …
options: reading the opening, the topic sentences and the close
steps.answer: reading the opening, the topic sentences and the close
steps.why: Skimming is selective, not merely fast.

steps.title: Lesson 21 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The period in the far north when the sun does not rise at all is …
steps.why: White nights and the midnight sun are the opposite phenomenon.

steps.title: Lesson 22 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Somebody who functions best late in the evening is …
steps.why: A night owl.

steps.title: Lesson 22 · listening
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The speaker describes a 'second winter'. It is …
options: the stretch when the sun never appears at all
the period when the light returns but it is still cold and snowy
the few weeks when the snow finally melts
steps.answer: the period when the light returns but it is still cold and snowy
steps.why: She counts it as one of the two she loves because of what is changing, not what it feels like.

steps.title: Lesson 23 · paraphrase
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: 'Such occurrences are coincidence.' Such occurrences refers to …
options: all tsunamis, whatever the phase of the moon
tsunamis happening at the same time as a supermoon
every supermoon, whether or not anything else happens
steps.answer: tsunamis happening at the same time as a supermoon
steps.why: The phrase points back to the pairing, not to either event alone.

steps.title: Lesson 23 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Two things happening at the same time by chance is …
steps.why: Coincidence.

steps.title: Lesson 24 · interrupting
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which interruption is most polite?
options: Sorry, that's wrong — you've misunderstood the proposal.
If I could just interrupt a second, I think that …
Wait a moment, would you listen to what I'm saying?
steps.answer: If I could just interrupt a second, I think that …
steps.why: It asks permission and softens with just before the point is made.

steps.title: Lesson 24 · holding the floor
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Somebody interrupts you mid-sentence. Which reclaims your turn without hostility?
options: If I could just finish what I was saying …
steps.answer: If I could just finish what I was saying …
steps.why: It marks the interruption and returns to the point in one move.

steps.title: Lesson 24 · listening
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Rjukan loses the sun for six months because of …
options: its latitude, like everywhere else that far north
its geography — a deep valley below a tall mountain
the cloud that sits over the valley all winter
steps.answer: its geography — a deep valley below a tall mountain
steps.why: Latitude alone would not do it; the mountain casts the shadow.

steps.title: Lessons 17 and 20 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is a prediction the speaker is not certain about?
steps.why: Probably + will marks it as a hedged prediction.

steps.title: Lessons 13 and 15 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
steps.why: Most people in general; most of the people about a defined group.

steps.title: Lessons 18 and 22 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which describes a habit rather than a single occasion?
options: I'm going to bed early tonight.
I tend to go to bed early.
steps.answer: I tend to go to bed early.
steps.why: Tend to marks a tendency.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To begin to understand and deal with something difficult is to …
steps.why: Get to grips with.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Money you pay into yourself for your retirement is …
steps.why: A private pension.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To fail to take a chance that was available is to …
steps.why: Miss out on. Turn down is an active refusal.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A district that is in poor condition and neglected is …
steps.why: Run-down.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · register
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is the most formal way of disagreeing?
steps.why: I beg to differ is markedly formal.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · function
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You want more thinking time in a meeting. Which is best?
options: That's a fair point — can I come back to you on that?
I don't know the answer to that yet.
Ask me again after the meeting.
steps.answer: That's a fair point — can I come back to you on that?
steps.why: It acknowledges the point and defers explicitly, which keeps the turn.

steps.title: Lesson 14 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'The scheme was set up ___ residents could share a kitchen and a laundry.'
steps.why: So that + a clause; so as to and in order to take an infinitive.

steps.title: Lesson 19 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Most people abandon a new habit …
options: between the second and fourth week
steps.answer: between the second and fourth week
steps.why: The stretch where the effort is the same and the visible progress is not.

steps.title: Chapters 4–6 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Time spent giving somebody your full attention is …
steps.why: Quality time.

steps.title: Урок пройден
